210	def _validate_request_record(record: object) -> dict:
211	    """Validate one persisted once-request record and return an independent copy.
212	
213	    A record carries exactly ``version`` (a non-negative JSON integer), ``root``
214	    (64 lowercase hex characters) and ``transfers`` (a non-empty array shaped like a
215	    :meth:`State.transfer_many` batch). Missing fields, extra fields or type
216	    confusion raise ``ValueError``.
217	    """
218	    if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record) != {"version", "root", "transfers"}:
219	        raise ValueError("corrupt request record: expected exactly version, root and transfers")
220	    version = record["version"]
221	    if not _is_int(version) or version < 0:
222	        raise ValueError("corrupt request record: version must be a non-negative integer")
223	    root = record["root"]
224	    if not _is_hex64(root):
225	        raise ValueError("corrupt request record: root must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
226	    transfers = _validate_transfers(record["transfers"])

230	def _validate_transfer_proof(proof: object) -> dict:
231	    """Validate the shape of a persisted transfer preview proof and return a deep copy.
232	
233	    Mirrors the structure :meth:`State.prove_transfers` emits: exactly ``root`` and
234	    ``new_root`` (64 lowercase hex characters), ``size`` (a positive JSON integer),
235	    ``items`` (strictly ascending non-empty names with non-negative JSON integer
236	    balances and in-range, strictly ascending indices) and ``nodes`` (strictly
237	    ascending ``(level, index)`` positions, levels and indices non-negative, each
238	    hash 64 lowercase hex characters). Anything malformed raises ``ValueError``;
239	    the cryptographic root checks live in :meth:`State.verify_transfers`.
240	    """
241	    if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != {
242	        "root", "new_root", "size", "items", "nodes"
243	    }:
244	        raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: expected exactly root, new_root, size, items and nodes")
245	    root = proof["root"]
246	    new_root = proof["new_root"]
247	    if not _is_hex64(root) or not _is_hex64(new_root):
248	        raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: roots must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
249	    size = proof["size"]
250	    if not _is_int(size) or size <= 0:
251	        raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: size must be a positive integer")
252	    raw_items = proof["items"]
253	    raw_nodes = proof["nodes"]
254	    if not isinstance(raw_items, list) or not isinstance(raw_nodes, list):
255	        raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: items and nodes must be arrays")
256	    items: list[dict] = []
257	    previous_name: str | None = None
258	    previous_index = -1
259	    for item in raw_items:
260	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"account", "balance", "index"}:
261	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: each item must hold exactly account, balance and index")
262	        name = item["account"]
263	        index = item["index"]
264	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
265	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: item accounts must be non-empty strings")
266	        if previous_name is not None and not previous_name < name:
267	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: items must be strictly ascending by name")
268	        if not _is_int(item["balance"]) or item["balance"] < 0:
269	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: item balances must be non-negative integers")
270	        if not _is_int(index) or not previous_index < index < size:
271	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: item indices must be strictly ascending and in range")
272	        items.append({"account": name, "balance": item["balance"], "index": index})
273	        previous_name, previous_index = name, index
274	    nodes: list[dict] = []
275	    previous_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
276	    for node in raw_nodes:
277	        if not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) != {"level", "index", "hash"}:
278	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: each node must hold exactly level, index and hash")
279	        level, index = node["level"], node["index"]
280	        if not _is_int(level) or not _is_int(index) or level < 0 or index < 0:
281	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: node level and index must be non-negative integers")
282	        position = (level, index)
283	        if previous_position is not None and not previous_position < position:
284	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: nodes must be strictly ascending by level then index")
285	        if not _is_hex64(node["hash"]):
286	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt proof: node hashes must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
287	        nodes.append({"level": level, "index": index, "hash": node["hash"]})
288	        previous_position = position
289	    return {"root": root, "new_root": new_root, "size": size,
290	            "items": items, "nodes": nodes}

293	def _validate_receipt(receipt: object) -> dict:
294	    """Validate one persisted settlement receipt and return an independent copy.
295	
296	    A receipt carries exactly ``version`` (a non-negative JSON integer),
297	    ``transfers`` (a non-empty batch shaped like a :meth:`State.transfer_many`
298	    batch) and ``proof`` (a transfer preview proof). Consistency with the
299	    matching success record and cryptographic verification of the proof against
300	    the record's old root are checked by :meth:`State.transfer_receipt`.
301	    Missing fields, extra fields or type confusion raise ``ValueError``.
302	    """
303	    if not isinstance(receipt, dict) or set(receipt) != {"version", "transfers", "proof"}:
304	        raise ValueError("corrupt receipt: expected exactly version, transfers and proof")
305	    version = receipt["version"]
306	    if not _is_int(version) or version < 0:
307	        raise ValueError("corrupt receipt: version must be a non-negative integer")
308	    transfers = _validate_transfers(receipt["transfers"])
309	    proof = _validate_transfer_proof(receipt["proof"])
310	    return {"version": version, "transfers": transfers, "proof": proof}

314	    """Validate one absence-proof boundary: a genuine inclusion proof strictly bracketing account."""
315	    name = boundary["account"]
316	    balance = boundary["balance"]

318	        return False
319	    if relation == "prev":
320	        if not name < account:
321	            return False
322	    elif not name > account:
323	        return False

328	class State:
329	    """A single-process account state machine rooted at ``root``."""
330	
331	    def __init__(self, root: str | Path) -> None:
332	        self.directory = Path(root)
333	        self.path = self.directory / STATE_FILE
334	
335	    # -- persistence ------------------------------------------------------------------
336	
337	    def init(self) -> None:
338	        """Create an empty state, replacing any existing one.
339	
340	        Snapshots, successful once-request records and their settlement receipts
341	        are reset along with the accounts and version.
342	        """
343	        self.directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
344	        self._write({"version": 0, "accounts": {}, SNAPSHOTS_KEY: {},
345	                     REQUESTS_KEY: {}, RECEIPTS_KEY: {}})
346	
347	    def _read(self) -> dict:
348	        if not self.path.is_file():
349	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no state at {self.path}; run init first")
350	        return json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
351	
352	    def _write(self, document: dict) -> None:
353	        """Atomically replace the state file, leaving the old one intact on failure.
354	
355	        The new document is fully written and flushed to a temporary file in the
356	        state directory, then renamed onto the state path. A failure anywhere in
357	        that sequence raises ``OSError`` without clobbering the existing state
358	        file.
359	        """
360	        self.directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
361	        payload = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
362	        # Match the permissions plain ``write_text`` would have used: keep an
363	        # existing file's mode, else apply the process umask to 0o666.
364	        try:
365	            mode = self.path.stat().st_mode & 0o777
366	        except FileNotFoundError:
367	            umask = os.umask(0)
368	            os.umask(umask)
369	            mode = 0o666 & ~umask
370	        temporary = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
371	            mode="w", encoding="utf-8", dir=self.directory, delete=False)
372	        try:
373	            temporary.write(payload)
374	            temporary.flush()
375	            os.fsync(temporary.fileno())
376	            temporary.close()
377	            os.chmod(temporary.name, mode)
378	            os.replace(temporary.name, self.path)
379	        except BaseException:
380	            temporary.close()
381	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
382	                os.unlink(temporary.name)
383	            raise

385	    @staticmethod
386	    def _snapshots(document: dict) -> dict:
387	        """The snapshot collection, treating a state file without one as empty.
388	
389	        A missing key is added to ``document`` so callers can persist new snapshots;
390	        a present-but-wrong-typed value is treated as corruption.
391	        """
392	        if SNAPSHOTS_KEY not in document:
393	            document[SNAPSHOTS_KEY] = {}
394	        snapshots = document[SNAPSHOTS_KEY]
395	        if not isinstance(snapshots, dict):
396	            raise ValueError("corrupt snapshots: expected a JSON object")

399	    @staticmethod
400	    def _requests(document: dict) -> dict:
401	        """The successful once-request records, treating a state file without them as empty.
402	
403	        A missing key is added to ``document`` so callers can persist new records;
404	        a present-but-wrong-typed value is treated as corruption. Records never
405	        participate in the state root and are not part of snapshots.
406	        """
407	        if REQUESTS_KEY not in document:
408	            document[REQUESTS_KEY] = {}
409	        requests = document[REQUESTS_KEY]
410	        if not isinstance(requests, dict):
411	            raise ValueError("corrupt request records: expected a JSON object")

414	    @staticmethod
415	    def _receipts(document: dict) -> dict:
416	        """The settlement receipts, treating a state file without them as empty.
417	
418	        A missing key is added to ``document`` so callers can persist new receipts;
419	        a present-but-wrong-typed value is treated as corruption. Receipts never
420	        participate in the state root, are not part of snapshots and are kept keyed
421	        by the same request id as the success records.
422	        """
423	        if RECEIPTS_KEY not in document:
424	            document[RECEIPTS_KEY] = {}
425	        receipts = document[RECEIPTS_KEY]

427	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipts: expected a JSON object")

432	    def set(self, account: str, balance: int) -> int:
433	        """Write ``balance`` for ``account`` and return the new version number."""
434	        if not isinstance(account, str) or not account:
435	            raise ValueError("account must be a non-empty string")
436	        if not isinstance(balance, int) or isinstance(balance, bool) or balance < 0:
437	            raise ValueError("balance must be a non-negative integer")
438	        document = self._read()
439	        document["accounts"][account] = balance
440	        document["version"] = int(document["version"]) + 1
441	        self._write(document)
442	        return document["version"]

444	    def get(self, account: str) -> int:
445	        """Balance of ``account``, or 0 when the account is unknown or was deleted."""
446	        return int(self._read()["accounts"].get(account, 0))

448	    def delete(self, account: str) -> int:
449	        """Remove an existing ``account`` and return the new version number.
450	
451	        Deleting an unknown account raises ``KeyError``; writing a zero balance is not a
452	        deletion, so a zero-balance account must be removed explicitly.
453	        """
454	        if not isinstance(account, str) or not account:
455	            raise ValueError("account must be a non-empty string")
456	        document = self._read()
457	        if account not in document["accounts"]:
458	            raise KeyError(f"unknown account {account!r}")
459	        del document["accounts"][account]
460	        document["version"] = int(document["version"]) + 1
461	        self._write(document)
462	        return document["version"]

464	    def apply(self, transaction: dict) -> int:
465	        """Apply one transaction of batched ``set`` writes and ``delete`` removals.
466	
467	        ``transaction`` is a JSON object with exactly two optional fields: ``set`` maps
468	        non-empty account names to non-negative integer balances (booleans are not
469	        integers), ``delete`` is an array of unique non-empty account names, none of
470	        which may also appear in ``set``. Every check runs before anything is written,
471	        so a rejected transaction leaves no visible change: malformed structure raises
472	        ``ValueError``; deleting an unknown account raises ``KeyError``. A non-empty
473	        batch commits atomically and adds exactly one version; an empty batch (both
474	        fields omitted or empty) returns the current version without writing.
475	        """
476	        if not isinstance(transaction, dict):
477	            raise ValueError("transaction must be a JSON object")
478	        extra = set(transaction) - {"set", "delete"}
479	        if extra:
480	            raise ValueError(f"unexpected transaction fields: {', '.join(sorted(extra))}")
481	        writes = transaction.get("set", {})
482	        removals = transaction.get("delete", [])
483	        if not isinstance(writes, dict):
484	            raise ValueError("transaction 'set' must be a JSON object")
485	        if not isinstance(removals, list):
486	            raise ValueError("transaction 'delete' must be a JSON array")
487	
488	        for account, balance in writes.items():
489	            if not isinstance(account, str) or not account:
490	                raise ValueError("account must be a non-empty string")
491	            if not isinstance(balance, int) or isinstance(balance, bool) or balance < 0:
492	                raise ValueError("balance must be a non-negative integer")
493	
494	        seen: set[str] = set()
495	        for account in removals:
496	            if not isinstance(account, str) or not account:
497	                raise ValueError("account must be a non-empty string")
498	            if account in seen:
499	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate delete for account {account!r}")
500	            if account in writes:
501	                raise ValueError(f"account {account!r} appears in both set and delete")
502	            seen.add(account)
503	
504	        document = self._read()
505	        accounts = document["accounts"]
506	        if not writes and not removals:
507	            return int(document["version"])
508	        for account in removals:
509	            if account not in accounts:
510	                raise KeyError(f"unknown account {account!r}")
511	        for account, balance in writes.items():
512	            accounts[account] = balance
513	        for account in removals:
514	            del accounts[account]
515	        document["version"] = int(document["version"]) + 1
516	        self._write(document)
517	        return document["version"]

519	    def transfer(self, source: str, target: str, amount: int) -> int:
520	        """Atomically move ``amount`` from ``source`` to ``target`` and return the new version.
521	
522	        ``source`` and ``target`` must be distinct non-empty strings and ``amount`` a
523	        positive JSON integer (booleans are not integers). ``source`` must already hold
524	        at least ``amount``; an unknown source raises ``KeyError`` and insufficient funds
525	        raise ``ValueError``. ``target`` is created with ``amount`` when absent or has it
526	        added to its balance; a source drained to zero keeps its account record. Every
527	        check runs before anything is written, so a rejected transfer leaves the
528	        accounts, version and state root untouched. A successful transfer adds exactly
529	        one version.
530	        """
531	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
532	            raise ValueError("source must be a non-empty string")
533	        if not isinstance(target, str) or not target:
534	            raise ValueError("target must be a non-empty string")
535	        if source == target:
536	            raise ValueError("source and target must be different accounts")
537	        if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
538	            raise ValueError("amount must be a positive integer")
539	        document = self._read()
540	        accounts = document["accounts"]
541	        if source not in accounts:
542	            raise KeyError(f"unknown account {source!r}")
543	        source_balance = int(accounts[source])
544	        if source_balance < amount:
545	            raise ValueError(
546	                f"insufficient funds: {source!r} has {source_balance}, needs {amount}"
547	            )
548	        accounts[source] = source_balance - amount
549	        accounts[target] = int(accounts.get(target, 0)) + amount
550	        document["version"] = int(document["version"]) + 1
551	        self._write(document)
552	        return document["version"]

554	    def transfer_many(self, batch: object) -> int:
555	        """Atomically settle a non-empty batch of transfers in order and return the new version.
556	
557	        ``batch`` is a non-empty JSON array; every item is an object carrying exactly
558	        ``source``, ``target`` and ``amount``, with distinct non-empty names and a
559	        positive JSON integer (booleans are not integers). Repeated transfers and
560	        accounts are allowed. Every endpoint must already exist -- a zero-balance
561	        account counts -- or ``KeyError`` is raised. Transfers settle in order, so a
562	        credit from one transfer is available to a later debit; each source must hold
563	        enough at its turn or ``ValueError`` is raised. Structure is validated before
564	        the state is read, so malformed input raises ``ValueError`` while an
565	        uninitialised state raises ``FileNotFoundError``. The batch adds exactly one
566	        version (even when every final balance equals its starting value), drained
567	        accounts keep their records, and a rejected batch changes neither the
568	        accounts, version, root nor snapshots.
569	        """
570	        normalized = _validate_transfers(batch)
571	        document = self._read()
572	        accounts = document["accounts"]
573	        for transfer in normalized:
574	            if transfer["source"] not in accounts:
575	                raise KeyError(f"unknown account {transfer['source']!r}")
576	            if transfer["target"] not in accounts:
577	                raise KeyError(f"unknown account {transfer['target']!r}")
578	        balances = {name: int(balance) for name, balance in accounts.items()}
579	        for transfer in normalized:
580	            source, target, amount = (transfer["source"], transfer["target"],
581	                                      transfer["amount"])
582	            if balances[source] < amount:
583	                raise ValueError(
584	                    f"insufficient funds: {source!r} has {balances[source]}, needs {amount}"
585	                )
586	            balances[source] -= amount
587	            balances[target] += amount
588	        for name, balance in balances.items():
589	            accounts[name] = balance
590	        document["version"] = int(document["version"]) + 1
591	        self._write(document)
592	        return document["version"]

594	    def transfer_many_once(self, request_id: object, expected_root: object, batch: object) -> int:
595	        """Idempotently settle a transfer batch under an old-root constraint.
596	
597	        ``request_id`` is a non-empty string identifying the request, ``expected_root``
598	        is the 64-lowercase-hex state root the state must currently carry, and
599	        ``batch`` follows the same rules and in-order settlement semantics as
600	        :meth:`transfer_many`. All three arguments are validated before the state is
601	        read, so malformed structure, types or root formatting raise ``ValueError``
602	        while a legal-but-uninitialised state raises ``FileNotFoundError``.
603	
604	        A first success requires the current root to equal ``expected_root``; it
605	        settles the whole batch in order, advances the version exactly once (even
606	        when every final balance is unchanged), records the request and saves a
607	        settlement receipt holding the same preview proof
608	        :meth:`prove_transfers` would return immediately before the commit. The
609	        return value is still just the new version; the receipt is read back via
610	        :meth:`transfer_receipt`. A repeat carrying the same id, old root and
611	        batch returns the first success's version without settling or writing,
612	        even if the accounts changed or a snapshot was restored in between; a
613	        repeat never (re)writes a receipt. Batch equality preserves array order
614	        and duplicates and ignores object key order. The same id with another
615	        old root or batch raises ``RuntimeError``; a new id against a mismatched
616	        current root raises ``RuntimeError`` as well. After the repeat check the
617	        old root is compared, then every endpoint is checked -- an unknown
618	        endpoint raises ``KeyError`` -- and only then does the batch settle,
619	        with an insufficient balance raising ``ValueError``. A failed attempt
620	        neither consumes the id nor mutates the input; accounts, root, version,
621	        snapshots, records and receipts all stay unchanged. The settled root
622	        equals the receipt proof's ``new_root`` (and the ``new_root``
623	        :meth:`prove_transfers` returns from the same old state); the root
624	        constraint is independent of the version. Accounts, the record and the
625	        receipt commit in one atomic write, so a write failure raises
626	        ``OSError`` and changes nothing.
627	        """
628	        if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
629	            raise ValueError("request id must be a non-empty string")
630	        if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
631	            raise ValueError("expected root must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
632	        normalized = _validate_transfers(batch)
633	
634	        document = self._read()
635	        accounts = document["accounts"]
636	        requests = self._requests(document)
637	        current_root = _root_for(accounts)
638	
639	        # Repeat requests win over every state-level check: a recorded success
640	        # replays its version regardless of later account changes or restores,
641	        # and never writes or backfills a receipt.
642	        if request_id in requests:
643	            saved = _validate_request_record(requests[request_id])
644	            if saved["root"] != expected_root or saved["transfers"] != normalized:
645	                raise RuntimeError(
646	                    f"request {request_id!r} already succeeded under a different root or batch"
647	                )
648	            return saved["version"]
649	
650	        if current_root != expected_root:
651	            raise RuntimeError(
652	                f"current root {current_root} does not match expected root {expected_root}"
653	            )
654	        # The preview performs the endpoint and in-order funds checks and yields
655	        # exactly the proof prove_transfers would emit from this old state.
656	        proof, balances = self._transfer_preview(document, normalized)
657	        for name, balance in balances.items():
658	            accounts[name] = balance
659	        document["version"] = int(document["version"]) + 1
660	        version = document["version"]
661	        requests[request_id] = {
662	            "version": version, "root": expected_root,
663	            "transfers": normalized}
664	        receipts = self._receipts(document)
665	        receipts[request_id] = {
666	            "version": version, "transfers": normalized, "proof": proof}
667	        self._write(document)
668	        return version

670	    def _transfer_preview(self, document: dict, normalized: list[dict]) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
671	        """Build the transfer preview proof for ``normalized`` over an unmutated document.
672	
673	        Returns the same proof object :meth:`prove_transfers` returns -- so a proof
674	        saved at commit time and one previewed beforehand compare equal as JSON --
675	        together with the settled name-to-balance mapping. Callers run their own
676	        root constraint before this; an unknown endpoint raises ``KeyError`` and an
677	        insufficient balance during in-order settlement raises ``ValueError``.
678	        """
679	        state_accounts = document["accounts"]
680	        for transfer in normalized:
681	            if transfer["source"] not in state_accounts:
682	                raise KeyError(f"unknown account {transfer['source']!r}")
683	            if transfer["target"] not in state_accounts:
684	                raise KeyError(f"unknown account {transfer['target']!r}")
685	        names = sorted(state_accounts)
686	        endpoint_names = {endpoint for transfer in normalized
687	                          for endpoint in (transfer["source"], transfer["target"])}
688	        chosen = sorted(names.index(name) for name in endpoint_names)
689	        leaves = [_leaf(n, int(state_accounts[n])) for n in names]
690	        items = [{"account": names[index], "balance": int(state_accounts[names[index]]),
691	                  "index": index} for index in chosen]
692	        root = merkle_root(leaves).hex()
693	        balances = {name: int(balance) for name, balance in state_accounts.items()}
694	        for transfer in normalized:
695	            source, target, amount = (transfer["source"], transfer["target"],
696	                                      transfer["amount"])
697	            if balances[source] < amount:
698	                raise ValueError(
699	                    f"insufficient funds: {source!r} has {balances[source]}, needs {amount}"
700	                )
701	            balances[source] -= amount
702	            balances[target] += amount
703	        new_leaves = list(leaves)
704	        for index in chosen:
705	            name = names[index]
706	            new_leaves[index] = _leaf(name, balances[name])
707	        new_root = merkle_root(new_leaves).hex()
708	        nodes = [{"level": level, "index": index, "hash": hash_value}
709	                 for level, index, hash_value in merkle_multiproof(leaves, chosen)]
710	        proof = {"root": root, "new_root": new_root, "size": len(names),
711	                 "items": items, "nodes": nodes}
712	        return proof, balances
713	
714	    def prove_transfers(self, batch: object) -> dict:
715	        """Read-only preview proof for an atomic transfer batch without writing.
716	
717	        ``batch`` follows the same rules as :meth:`transfer_many`; structure and types
718	        are validated before the state is read (``ValueError``), an uninitialised state
719	        raises ``FileNotFoundError``, an unknown endpoint raises ``KeyError`` and an
720	        insufficient balance raises ``ValueError``. The proof carries the current
721	        ``root``, the ``new_root`` after settling the whole batch in order, the total
722	        ``size``, one ``items`` entry per de-duplicated endpoint holding its *old*
723	        balance in the same compact layout as :meth:`prove_many`, and the minimal
724	        ``nodes`` shared by both trees. Proving a batch whose endpoints cover every
725	        account yields empty ``nodes``; when every final balance equals the old one the
726	        two roots are equal. Nothing is persisted and the input array is never modified.
727	        """
728	        normalized = _validate_transfers(batch)
729	        document = self._read()
730	        proof, _ = self._transfer_preview(document, normalized)
731	        return proof
732	
733	    def verify_transfers(self, batch: object, expected_root: object, proof: object) -> bool:
734	        """Verify a transfer-batch preview proof using the proof alone; no state is read.
735	
736	        Only a proof isomorphic to one :meth:`prove_transfers` emits is accepted: a JSON
737	        object with exactly ``root``, ``new_root``, ``size``, ``items`` and ``nodes``.
738	        The ``batch`` must be a valid non-empty transfer array, the endpoint de-dup set
739	        must equal the proven accounts, and ``root`` must equal the trusted 64-lowercase
740	        hex ``expected_root``. Items carry the strictly ascending old-balance entries in
741	        the same compact layout as :meth:`verify_many`; the minimal nodes must recompute
742	        ``root`` from the old leaves and ``new_root`` from the same leaves after the
743	        whole batch settles in order with every per-transfer debit covered, consuming
744	        every node exactly once in each recomputation. Invalid arguments, missing or
745	        extra fields, a set mismatch, type confusion (including booleans), out-of-order
746	        entries, out-of-range indices, insufficient balances, missing, duplicate or
747	        surplus nodes, or either root being wrong returns False.
748	        """
749	        try:
750	            normalized = _validate_transfers(batch)
751	            if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
752	                return False
753	            if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != {
754	                "root", "new_root", "size", "items", "nodes"
755	            }:
756	                return False
757	            root = proof["root"]
758	            new_root = proof["new_root"]
759	            if not _is_hex64(root) or root != expected_root or not _is_hex64(new_root):
760	                return False
761	            size = proof["size"]
762	            raw_items = proof["items"]
763	            raw_nodes = proof["nodes"]
764	            if (not _is_int(size) or size <= 0 or not isinstance(raw_items, list)
765	                    or not isinstance(raw_nodes, list)):
766	                return False
767	            endpoints = {endpoint for transfer in normalized
768	                         for endpoint in (transfer["source"], transfer["target"])}
769	            if len(raw_items) != len(endpoints):
770	                return False
771	
772	            old_leaves: dict[int, bytes] = {}
773	            old_balances: dict[str, int] = {}
774	            previous_name: str | None = None
775	            previous_index = -1
776	            for item in raw_items:
777	                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"account", "balance", "index"}:
778	                    return False
779	                name = item["account"]
780	                index = item["index"]
781	                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
782	                    return False
783	                if previous_name is not None and not previous_name < name:
784	                    return False
785	                if not _is_int(item["balance"]) or item["balance"] < 0:
786	                    return False
787	                if not _is_int(index) or not previous_index < index < size:
788	                    return False
789	                old_leaves[index] = _leaf(name, item["balance"])
790	                old_balances[name] = item["balance"]
791	                previous_name, previous_index = name, index
792	            if {item["account"] for item in raw_items} != endpoints:
793	                return False
794	
795	            balances = dict(old_balances)
796	            for transfer in normalized:
797	                source, target, amount = (transfer["source"], transfer["target"],
798	                                          transfer["amount"])
799	                if balances[source] < amount:
800	                    return False
801	                balances[source] -= amount
802	                balances[target] += amount
803	
804	            nodes: dict[tuple[int, int], bytes] = {}
805	            previous_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
806	            for node in raw_nodes:
807	                if not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) != {"level", "index", "hash"}:
808	                    return False
809	                level, index = node["level"], node["index"]
810	                if not _is_int(level) or not _is_int(index) or level < 0 or index < 0:
811	                    return False
812	                position = (level, index)
813	                if previous_position is not None and not previous_position < position:
814	                    return False

832	    def transfer_receipt(self, request_id: object) -> dict | None:
833	        """Return the historical settlement receipt for a once-request, or None.

836	        a build that saved receipts; an older success record without a receipt
837	        yields ``None`` and is never backfilled, neither here nor on a repeat
838	        commit. The returned object carries exactly ``request_id``, ``version``,
839	        ``transfers`` and ``proof``: the identifier, version and batch of the
840	        first successful settlement (the batch preserves order and duplicates),
841	        and the preview proof saved at commit time. The proof equals the one
842	        :meth:`prove_transfers` returned before the commit as JSON content, and
843	        its ``new_root`` is the state root right after that settlement, so it
844	        verifies through :meth:`verify_transfers` together with the batch and
845	        the record's trusted old root long after later account changes or
846	        snapshot restores.

849	        against an uninitialised state raises ``FileNotFoundError`` and an
850	        unknown identifier raises ``KeyError``. A persisted receipt with illegal
851	        fields or types, one whose id/version/batch do not match the success
852	        record, or one whose proof cannot be verified against the record's old
853	        root raises ``ValueError`` -- corruption is never reported as a missing
854	        receipt. The result is an independent deep copy; the query neither
855	        writes nor advances the version.

863	        record = _validate_request_record(requests[request_id])
864	        receipts = self._receipts(document)
865	        if request_id not in receipts:
866	            # An older success record never gets a backfilled receipt.
867	            return None
868	        receipt = _validate_receipt(receipts[request_id])
869	        if receipt["version"] != record["version"] or receipt["transfers"] != record["transfers"]:
870	            raise ValueError("corrupt receipt: version or transfers do not match the success record")

872	        if not self.verify_transfers(receipt["transfers"], record["root"], proof):

875	                "transfers": receipt["transfers"], "proof": proof}

    def verify_many(self, accounts: object, expected_root: object, proof: object) -> bool:
        """Verify a compact multi-account inclusion proof using the proof alone.

        Only a proof isomorphic to one :meth:`prove_many` emits is accepted: a JSON
        object with exactly ``root``, ``size``, ``items`` and ``nodes``. The query
        ``accounts`` must be a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings equal as a
        set to the proven accounts; ``expected_root`` must equal the proof root. Items
        must be strictly ascending by name and by in-range index with non-negative
        integer balances, and nodes must be strictly ascending ``(level, index)``
        positions carrying 64 lowercase hex hashes. Every node must be a valid
        position, be consumed exactly once while recomputing the root and leave no
        surplus; duplicate or reconstructable nodes, out-of-range positions, a query
        mismatch or any root discrepancy return False. The state directory is never
        read.
        """
        try:
            normalized = _validate_account_set(accounts)
            if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
                return False
            if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != {"root", "size", "items", "nodes"}:
                return False
            root = proof["root"]
            if not _is_hex64(root) or root != expected_root:
                return False
            size = proof["size"]
            if not _is_int(size) or size <= 0:
                return False
            raw_items = proof["items"]
            raw_nodes = proof["nodes"]
            if not isinstance(raw_items, list) or not isinstance(raw_nodes, list):
                return False
            if len(raw_items) != len(normalized):
                return False

            leaves: dict[int, bytes] = {}
            previous_name: str | None = None
            previous_index = -1
            for item in raw_items:
                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"account", "balance", "index"}:
                    return False
                name = item["account"]
                index = item["index"]
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                    return False
                if previous_name is not None and not previous_name < name:
                    return False
                if not _is_int(item["balance"]) or item["balance"] < 0:
                    return False
                if not _is_int(index) or not previous_index < index < size:
                    return False
                leaves[index] = _leaf(name, item["balance"])
                previous_name, previous_index = name, index
            if {item["account"] for item in raw_items} != set(normalized):
                return False

            nodes: dict[tuple[int, int], bytes] = {}
            previous_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
            for node in raw_nodes:
                if not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) != {"level", "index", "hash"}:
                    return False
                level, index = node["level"], node["index"]
                if not _is_int(level) or not _is_int(index) or level < 0 or index < 0:
                    return False
                position = (level, index)
                if previous_position is not None and not previous_position < position:
                    return False
                if not _is_hex64(node["hash"]):
                    return False
                nodes[position] = bytes.fromhex(node["hash"])
                previous_position = position

            recomputed = merkle_verify_multiproof(leaves, nodes, size)
            return recomputed is not None and recomputed.hex() == root
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return False

    def prove_lookup(self, accounts: object) -> dict:
        """Compact existence/absence lookup proof for a non-empty set of accounts.

        ``accounts`` must be an array of unique non-empty strings (order is free);
        malformed structure, wrong types or duplicate names raise ``ValueError``.
        Unknown accounts are a normal result rather than an error. The proof carries
        the state root, the full tree ``size``, one ``result`` per queried account in
        ascending name order, and the same compact ``items``/``nodes`` layout as
        :meth:`prove_many`: items cover the de-duplicated union of the existing
        queries and the predecessor/successor boundaries the absent queries need,
        and one shared multi-proof connects every item to the root. An existing
        account (zero balance included) yields its full-sorted index with null
        ``prev``/``next``; an absent one yields null ``index`` and the immediate
        neighbour indices (null past either end). An empty state yields the
        empty-tree root, size 0 and no items or nodes. Generation never mutates
        accounts, versions, the root or snapshots.
        """
        normalized = _validate_account_set(accounts)
        document = self._read()
        state_accounts = document["accounts"]
        names = sorted(state_accounts)
        size = len(names)
        leaves = [_leaf(n, int(state_accounts[n])) for n in names]
        results: list[dict] = []
        needed: set[int] = set()
        for account in sorted(normalized):
            position = bisect.bisect_left(names, account)
            if position < size and names[position] == account:
                results.append({"account": account, "index": position,
                                "prev": None, "next": None})
                needed.add(position)
            else:
                prev_index = position - 1 if position > 0 else None
                next_index = position if position < size else None
                results.append({"account": account, "index": None,
                                "prev": prev_index, "next": next_index})
                if prev_index is not None:
                    needed.add(prev_index)
                if next_index is not None:
                    needed.add(next_index)
        chosen = sorted(needed)
        items = [{"account": names[index], "balance": int(state_accounts[names[index]]),
                  "index": index} for index in chosen]
        nodes = [{"level": level, "index": index, "hash": hash_value}
                 for level, index, hash_value in merkle_multiproof(leaves, chosen)]
        return {"root": _root_for(state_accounts), "size": size,
                "results": results, "items": items, "nodes": nodes}

    def verify_lookup(self, accounts: object, expected_root: object, proof: object) -> bool:
        """Verify a compact existence/absence lookup proof using the proof alone.

        Only a proof isomorphic to one :meth:`prove_lookup` emits is accepted: a JSON
        object with exactly ``root``, ``size``, ``results``, ``items`` and ``nodes``.
        The query ``accounts`` must be a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings
        and ``results`` must answer them in strictly ascending name order. An
        existing result carries a non-null in-range index with null neighbours and a
        same-name, same-index inclusion item; an absent result carries a null index
        and adjacent predecessor/successor indices (null past the ends, with the
        same strict-bracketing and adjacency rules as :meth:`verify_absence`), each
        backed by an inclusion item. ``items`` must equal exactly the de-duplicated
        union of existing accounts and referenced boundaries -- no missing or
        unrelated entries -- and ``nodes`` must be the minimal shared multi-proof
        that recomputes a root equal to both ``proof.root`` and ``expected_root``.
        Size 0 is anchored solely by the empty-tree root with every result null.
        Type confusion (including booleans posing as integers), missing or extra
        fields, or any other inconsistency return False; the state directory is
        never read.
        """
        try:
            normalized = _validate_account_set(accounts)
            if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
                return False
            if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != {
                "root", "size", "results", "items", "nodes"
            }:
                return False
            root = proof["root"]
            if not _is_hex64(root) or root != expected_root:
                return False
            size = proof["size"]
            if not _is_int(size) or size < 0:
                return False
            raw_results = proof["results"]
            raw_items = proof["items"]
            raw_nodes = proof["nodes"]
            if (not isinstance(raw_results, list) or not isinstance(raw_items, list)
                    or not isinstance(raw_nodes, list)):
                return False
            if len(raw_results) != len(normalized):
                return False

            if size == 0:
                if raw_items or raw_nodes or root != merkle_root([]).hex():
                    return False
                for result, account in zip(raw_results, sorted(normalized)):
                    if (not isinstance(result, dict)
                            or set(result) != {"account", "index", "prev", "next"}
                            or result["account"] != account
                            or result["index"] is not None
                            or result["prev"] is not None
                            or result["next"] is not None):
                        return False
                return True

            # Validate results and collect the item indices each result requires.
            required: set[int] = set()
            specs: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
            for result, account in zip(raw_results, sorted(normalized)):
                if (not isinstance(result, dict)
                        or set(result) != {"account", "index", "prev", "next"}
                        or result["account"] != account):
                    return False
                index, previous, following = result["index"], result["prev"], result["next"]
                if index is not None:
                    if (not _is_int(index) or not 0 <= index < size
                            or previous is not None or following is not None):
                        return False
                    required.add(index)
                    specs.append((account, index, index))
                    continue
                if previous is not None and (not _is_int(previous) or not 0 <= previous < size):
                    return False
                if following is not None and (not _is_int(following) or not 0 <= following < size):
                    return False
                prev_index = -1 if previous is None else previous
                next_index = size if following is None else following
                if next_index != prev_index + 1:
                    return False
                if previous is not None:
                    required.add(previous)
                if following is not None:
                    required.add(following)
                specs.append((account, prev_index, next_index))

            # Validate inclusion items and index them by leaf position.
            leaves: dict[int, bytes] = {}
            item_names: dict[int, str] = {}
            previous_name: str | None = None
            previous_index = -1
            for item in raw_items:
                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"account", "balance", "index"}:
                    return False
                name = item["account"]
                index = item["index"]
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                    return False
                if previous_name is not None and not previous_name < name:
                    return False
                if not _is_int(item["balance"]) or item["balance"] < 0:
                    return False
                if not _is_int(index) or not previous_index < index < size:
                    return False
                leaves[index] = _leaf(name, item["balance"])
                item_names[index] = name
                previous_name, previous_index = name, index
            if set(item_names) != required:
                return False

            # Existing results need a same-name item; absent ones need strict bracketing.
            for account, prev_index, next_index in specs:
                if prev_index == next_index:
                    if item_names[prev_index] != account:
                        return False
                else:
                    if prev_index >= 0 and not item_names[prev_index] < account:
                        return False
                    if next_index < size and not item_names[next_index] > account:
                        return False

            nodes: dict[tuple[int, int], bytes] = {}
            previous_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
            for node in raw_nodes:
                if not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) != {"level", "index", "hash"}:
                    return False
                level, index = node["level"], node["index"]
                if not _is_int(level) or not _is_int(index) or level < 0 or index < 0:
                    return False
                position = (level, index)
                if previous_position is not None and not previous_position < position:
                    return False
                if not _is_hex64(node["hash"]):
                    return False
                nodes[position] = bytes.fromhex(node["hash"])
                previous_position = position

            recomputed = merkle_verify_multiproof(leaves, nodes, size)
            return recomputed is not None and recomputed.hex() == root
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return False

            needed.add(prev_index)
        if next_index is not None:
            needed.add(next_index)
        nodes = [{"level": level, "index": index, "hash": hash_value}
                 for level, index, hash_value in merkle_multiproof(leaves, sorted(needed))]
        return {"start": start, "limit": limit, "root": root, "size": size,
                "prev": entry(prev_index),
                "next": entry(next_index) if next_index is not None else None,
                "items": items, "nodes": nodes}

    def verify_page(self, start: object, limit: object, expected_root: object, proof: object) -> bool:
        """Verify a name-paginated proof using the proof alone; no state is read.

        Only a proof isomorphic to one :meth:`prove_page` emits is accepted: a JSON
        object with exactly ``start``, ``limit``, ``root``, ``size``, ``prev``,
        ``next``, ``items`` and ``nodes``, with the query fields equal to the
        arguments. ``items`` must be strictly ascending by name and by continuous
        full-list index beginning at the first account at or past ``start``, each
        name at or above ``start`` with a non-negative integer balance; ``prev``
        (null before the first slot) must be an included account strictly below
        ``start`` at the index immediately before the page, and ``next`` (null when
        the page is partial or at the tail) an included account strictly after the
        last item at the immediately following index. The page may hold at most
        ``limit`` items and a short page forces ``next`` to be null. The items plus
        the non-null boundaries must be exactly the proven leaves, and the minimal
        shared multi-proof must consume every node and recompute a root equal to
        both ``proof.root`` and ``expected_root``. Size 0 is anchored solely by the
        empty-tree root with both boundaries null and empty arrays. Type confusion
        (including booleans posing as integers), missing or extra fields, gaps,
        out-of-order names, surplus nodes or any other inconsistency return False.
        """
        try:
            if not isinstance(start, str):
                return False
            if not _is_int(limit) or limit <= 0:
                return False
            if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
                return False
            if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != {
                "start", "limit", "root", "size", "prev", "next", "items", "nodes"
            }:
                return False
            if proof["start"] != start:
                return False
            proven_limit = proof["limit"]
            if not _is_int(proven_limit) or proven_limit != limit:
                return False
            root = proof["root"]
            if not _is_hex64(root) or root != expected_root:
                return False
            size = proof["size"]
            if not _is_int(size) or size < 0:
                return False
            previous, following, raw_items, raw_nodes = (
                proof["prev"], proof["next"], proof["items"], proof["nodes"])
            if not isinstance(raw_items, list) or not isinstance(raw_nodes, list):
                return False
            if len(raw_items) > limit:
                return False

            if size == 0:
                return (previous is None and following is None and not raw_items
                        and not raw_nodes and root == merkle_root([]).hex())

            def check_entry(boundary: object) -> dict | None:
                """Validate one compact inclusion entry, returning normalized fields."""
                if not isinstance(boundary, dict) or set(boundary) != {
                    "account", "balance", "index"
                }:
                    return None
                name = boundary["account"]
                index = boundary["index"]
                balance = boundary["balance"]
                if (not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(index)
                        or not 0 <= index < size or not _is_int(balance) or balance < 0):
                    return None
                return {"account": name, "balance": balance, "index": index}

            prev_entry = check_entry(previous) if previous is not None else None
            if previous is not None and prev_entry is None:
                return False
            next_entry = check_entry(following) if following is not None else None
            if following is not None and next_entry is None:
                return False

            page_start = 0 if prev_entry is None else prev_entry["index"] + 1
            page_end = size - 1 if next_entry is None else next_entry["index"] - 1
            expected_count = max(0, page_end - page_start + 1)
            if expected_count != len(raw_items) or expected_count > limit:
                return False
            # A short (partial) page is the unique end signal: next must then be null.
            if expected_count < limit and next_entry is not None:
                return False
            # page_start/page_end are pinned by the boundaries; the count equality and
            # continuous item indices below force prev/next to sit adjacent to the page.
            if prev_entry is not None and not prev_entry["account"] < start:
                return False

            leaves: dict[int, bytes] = {}
            item_names: dict[int, str] = {}
            last_name: str | None = None
            for position, item in enumerate(raw_items):
                checked = check_entry(item)
                if checked is None:
                    return False
                name, balance, index = (checked["account"], checked["balance"],
                                        checked["index"])
                if index != page_start + position:
                    return False
                if not name >= start:
                    return False
                if last_name is not None and not last_name < name:
                    return False
                leaves[index] = _leaf(name, balance)
                item_names[index] = name
                last_name = name
            if next_entry is not None:
                anchor_name = item_names[page_end] if raw_items else start
                if not next_entry["account"] > anchor_name:
                    return False

            if prev_entry is not None:
                index = prev_entry["index"]
                if index in leaves:
                    return False
                leaves[index] = _leaf(prev_entry["account"], prev_entry["balance"])
            if next_entry is not None:
                index = next_entry["index"]
                if index in leaves:
                    return False
                leaves[index] = _leaf(next_entry["account"], next_entry["balance"])

            nodes: dict[tuple[int, int], bytes] = {}
            previous_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
            for node in raw_nodes:
                if not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) != {"level", "index", "hash"}:
                    return False
                level, node_index = node["level"], node["index"]
                if not _is_int(level) or not _is_int(node_index) or level < 0 or node_index < 0:
                    return False
                position = (level, node_index)
                if previous_position is not None and not previous_position < position:
                    return False
                if not _is_hex64(node["hash"]):
                    return False
                nodes[position] = bytes.fromhex(node["hash"])
                previous_position = position

            recomputed = merkle_verify_multiproof(leaves, nodes, size)
            return recomputed is not None and recomputed.hex() == root
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return False

    def prove_update(self, updates: object) -> dict:
        """Read-only preview proof for replacing balances without writing.

        ``updates`` is a non-empty JSON object mapping non-empty account names to
        non-negative JSON integers (booleans are not integers). Every named account
        must already exist -- a zero-balance account counts -- or ``KeyError`` is
        raised; malformed structure or types raise ``ValueError`` before the state is
        read, and an uninitialised state raises ``FileNotFoundError``. The proof
        carries the current ``root``, ``new_root`` (the root after replacing only the
        named balances), the total ``size``, one ``items`` entry per updated account
        holding its *old* balance in the same compact layout as :meth:`prove_many`,
        and the minimal ``nodes`` shared by both trees. Updating every account yields
        empty ``nodes``; when every new balance equals the old one the two roots are
        equal. Nothing is persisted and the input object is never modified.
        """
        normalized = _validate_updates(updates)
        document = self._read()
        state_accounts = document["accounts"]
        for account in normalized:
            if account not in state_accounts:
                raise KeyError(f"unknown account {account!r}")
        names = sorted(state_accounts)
        chosen = sorted(names.index(account) for account in normalized)
        leaves = [_leaf(n, int(state_accounts[n])) for n in names]
        items = [{"account": names[index], "balance": int(state_accounts[names[index]]),
                  "index": index} for index in chosen]
        root = merkle_root(leaves).hex()
        new_leaves = list(leaves)
        for account, balance in normalized.items():
            new_leaves[names.index(account)] = _leaf(account, balance)
        new_root = merkle_root(new_leaves).hex()
        nodes = [{"level": level, "index": index, "hash": hash_value}
                 for level, index, hash_value in merkle_multiproof(leaves, chosen)]
        return {"root": root, "new_root": new_root, "size": len(names),
                "items": items, "nodes": nodes}

    def verify_update(self, updates: object, expected_root: object, proof: object) -> bool:
        """Verify a balance-update preview proof using the proof alone; no state is read.

        Only a proof isomorphic to one :meth:`prove_update` emits is accepted: a JSON
        object with exactly ``root``, ``new_root``, ``size``, ``items`` and
        ``nodes``. The ``updates`` object must be valid and equal as a set to the
        proven accounts, and ``root`` must equal the trusted ``expected_root``.
        Items carry the strictly ascending old-balance entries in the same compact
        layout as :meth:`verify_many`; the minimal nodes must recompute ``root`` from
        the old leaves and ``new_root`` from the same leaves with the named balances
        replaced, consuming every node exactly once in each recomputation. The
        supplied nodes anchor the new tree because each needed sibling subtree
        contains none of the updated accounts, so its hash is unchanged. Invalid
        arguments, missing or extra fields, a set mismatch, type confusion
        (including booleans), out-of-order entries, out-of-range indices, missing,
        duplicate or surplus nodes, or either root being wrong returns False.
        """
        try:
            normalized = _validate_updates(updates)
            if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
                return False
            if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != {
                "root", "new_root", "size", "items", "nodes"
            }:
                return False
            root = proof["root"]
            new_root = proof["new_root"]
            if not _is_hex64(root) or root != expected_root or not _is_hex64(new_root):
                return False
            size = proof["size"]
            raw_items = proof["items"]
            raw_nodes = proof["nodes"]
            if (not _is_int(size) or size <= 0 or not isinstance(raw_items, list)
                    or not isinstance(raw_nodes, list)):
                return False
            if len(raw_items) != len(normalized):
                return False

            old_leaves: dict[int, bytes] = {}
            previous_name: str | None = None
            previous_index = -1
            for item in raw_items:
                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"account", "balance", "index"}:
                    return False
                name = item["account"]
                index = item["index"]
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                    return False
                if previous_name is not None and not previous_name < name:
                    return False
                if not _is_int(item["balance"]) or item["balance"] < 0:
                    return False
                if not _is_int(index) or not previous_index < index < size:
                    return False
                old_leaves[index] = _leaf(name, item["balance"])
                previous_name, previous_index = name, index
            if {item["account"] for item in raw_items} != set(normalized):
                return False

            nodes: dict[tuple[int, int], bytes] = {}
            previous_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
            for node in raw_nodes:
                if not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) != {"level", "index", "hash"}:
                    return False
                level, index = node["level"], node["index"]
                if not _is_int(level) or not _is_int(index) or level < 0 or index < 0:
                    return False
                position = (level, index)
                if previous_position is not None and not previous_position < position:
                    return False
                if not _is_hex64(node["hash"]):
                    return False
                nodes[position] = bytes.fromhex(node["hash"])
                previous_position = position

            old_root = merkle_verify_multiproof(old_leaves, nodes, size)
            if old_root is None or old_root.hex() != root:
                return False
            new_leaves = dict(old_leaves)
            for item in raw_items:
                new_leaves[item["index"]] = _leaf(item["account"],
                                                  normalized[item["account"]])
            rebuilt = merkle_verify_multiproof(new_leaves, nodes, size)
            return rebuilt is not None and rebuilt.hex() == new_root
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return False
